description.value: A two-part pilot study examined whether direction-independent frontal and frontotemporal asymmetry in bvFTD contributes to socioemotional dysfunction using MRI measures and socioemotional scales.

spans.text: In a two-part study, we evaluated patients who met Clinical Consensus Criteria for bvFTD using socioemotional scales and magnetic and resonance imaging measures.

value: We hypothesize that differences in interhemispheric atrophy and its impact on the relationship between frontotemporal regions plays a significant role in socioemotional dysfunction, as evidenced in bvFTD.

description.value: A two-part observational evaluation of patients with clinically probable bvFTD; Part A included 18 patients and Part B included 24 patients, with MRI and socioemotional assessments.

spans.text: This study assesses measures of socioemotional functions and correlates them with the degree of frontal and frontotemporal asymmetry on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in a two-part evaluation of patients with bvFTD.
